text:
The defendant who hated her husband, saw the armed man waiting outside, and deliberately chose not to warn him is most likely guilty of murder. Her intent to see him die supplies the malice, and her silence was a deliberate choice rather than a lapse, though an omission conviction can turn on whether she had a legal duty to act. The other scenario, lending a car to an intoxicated friend who then causes a fatal crash, points to negligence or vehicular homicide, not murder, and my earlier general answer did not address either option.

CONFIDENCE: 70
